finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml::github app installation token is persisted into .git/config of the untrusted branch checkout, then branch-controlled install scripts are executed
evidence: Verified against the supplied files: in `.github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml` the `actions/checkout@v4` step passes `token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}` with `ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}` and no `persist-credentials: false`, so the App installation token is written into `.git/config` as an http.extraheader in the untrusted branch checkout; a later step then runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` on that branch tree, and root `package.json` does declare a `postinstall` script, so branch-controlled lifecycle scripts (and any branch-added dependency's install scripts) execute with the token readable via `git config --get http.https://github.com/.extraheader`. The contrast the reviewer draws is also accurate: `agent-review-panel.yml`'s `deps` and `review-panel` checkouts explicitly set `persist-credentials: false` with a comment giving exactly this reason, the panel's `fix` checkout does not, and the iterate job's App token is minted with no `permission-*` scoping (unlike the panel's contents/PR/issues-scoped token). Mitigating context (base-repo `agent/` branches only, `AGENT_PIPELINE_ENABLED`, `environment: agent`, and the fact that claude-code-action later receives the same token anyway) reduces but does not eliminate the exposure — it widens the leak to third-party install scripts and violates the repo's own stated rule; note this is pre-existing code, not introduced by the diff under review.
